title: Island Hopper
src: Flipkart Data Engineer OA (IIT BHU, handwritten)
body:
A grid has land cells and water cells. The hero stands on a land cell on the edge of an island and wants to reach any land cell inside the safe zone.

The hero cannot walk on land. He moves only by stepping into a 4-neighbouring water cell. His first move must go from his land cell into water, and his last move must step out of water onto a safe-zone land cell.

Each step onto a water cell costs health, and the cost grows: the 1st water step costs 2, the 2nd costs 4, the 3rd costs 6, and so on. So s water steps cost 2 + 4 + … + 2s = s(s + 1).

The hero has initial health Z. If he can reach the safe zone with health ≥ 0 left, print the largest health he can have left. If every route costs more than Z, print died and the extra health he would need on the cheapest route. If no route exists, print unreachable.

Reconstructed from a handwritten report; the grid symbols and output words were chosen for this mock.

Function to complete

Complete islandHopper(grid, r, c, Z). It returns the remaining health as a string, or "died X", or "unreachable".

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: m n. Next m lines: the grid, using . for water, # for land and * for land inside the safe zone. Then a line r c (0-indexed start, a # cell next to water), then a line with Z.
out: The remaining health, or died X, or unreachable.
cons: 1 ≤ m, n ≤ 1000 in the report (this mock tests up to 200 × 200)

samples.ex: The shortest water route is (0,1) (1,1) (2,1) (2,2) (2,3) (2,4) (1,4): 7 water steps, which cost 7 × 8 = 56. From (1,4) he steps onto the safe cell (0,4) with 60 − 56 = 4 health.
The same route costs 56, which is 36 more than his 20 health.
